name: Collected Mineral
subtitle: Warm mineral architecture, your collected RH furniture and thoughtfully chosen new pieces.
summary: A new complete home built around all 39 owned pieces: neutral mineral walls, natural oak, pale stone and restrained walnut. Brown oak and polished silver are concentrated in purposeful furniture groups; new furnishings complete the great room, office, cinema, formal dining, piano salon, guest rooms and terrace.
globalNotes: Owned inventory is allocated once across the home; new items are separate purchases.
Every camera has a paired day/night view. Unchanged views retain the approved Mineral & Walnut envelope; visible furniture glimpses through doors and mirrors are updated to this option.
Exact selected stock, quantity and delivery to ZIP 20878 must be confirmed before purchasing; dated catalog observations are not reservations.
Renders are design studies, not manufacturer CAD or measured construction drawings.
The penthouse bedroom remains unbuilt; its views depict proposed construction.
No bedroom color accents, stair runners or Option 2 blue/yellow palette. Approved stone-look wet-room materials remain.

materials.finish: Premium washable matte acrylic in warm ivory; warm ivory low-sheen trim enamel on painted doors, casings and baseboards.
materials.substratePreparation: Inspect for moisture, movement, uneven patches and incompatible existing coatings. Repair and skim as needed, sand and prime with the selected system. Protect glass, hardware and adjoining stone.
materials.installation: Separate wall coating from door/trim enamel. Use continuous finish boundaries at corners and trim, with no unexplained bright-white patches. Confirm physical color against the oak and walnut.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve the actual material, adjoining finishes and a representative installed sample in daylight and the specified warm evening lighting before ordering the full quantity.
materials.care: Use the selected manufacturer's cleaning and repair instructions; retain product data and matching touch-up material.

materials.finish: Restrained warm mushroom mineral/plaster appearance, with smooth low-contrast movement. Roman Clay is a dry-wall finish option, not a blanket requirement.
materials.substratePreparation: Produce a smooth, sound, properly primed dry wall following the selected coating supplier and the global mineral-finish rule. Resolve cracks, old coating compatibility and uneven absorption before the decorative coat.
materials.installation: Apply the complete selected decorative system to an approved large sample with its intended final sheen. Observe the global dry/wet and material-use boundaries; do not substitute this decorative finish for tile or waterproofing.
materials.sampleApproval: Sample the actual contractor's technique. Reject coarse ridges, peach/pink casts or dramatic clouds inconsistent with the approved room.
materials.care: Follow the finish supplier's dry-area care instructions; plan local repairs with an approved test patch because touch-ups may remain visible.

materials.surface: Entry gallery and center hall matched to the second floor
materials.finish: Matte natural neutral oak with restrained grain and low color variation, matched to the approved second-floor sample. Prefer a suitable engineered product after substrate review.
materials.substratePreparation: Survey existing floor build-up, subfloor condition, flatness, moisture, acoustic requirements, door clearances and transitions. Select the installation and underlayment with the flooring supplier; do not infer requirements from rendered color.
materials.installation: Coordinate continuous levels at thresholds, stair nosings and cabinets. Install per the flooring manufacturer, protect completed floors, and fit neutral loose rugs with a pad expressly compatible with the floor finish.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve a representative plank group beside warm ivory, mushroom mineral and walnut samples. The existing second-floor color is the reference.
materials.care: Use the floor manufacturer's care and felt-protection guidance. Rugs must not trap incompatible rubber, dyes or moisture against the finish.

lighting.day: Daylight is the main ambient source; chandelier and existing recessed positions supplement it only as needed.
lighting.night: Soft cascade glow and restrained existing circulation light; no new bright ceiling outline. Close actual entry-glass privacy coverage after dark when needed.
lighting.colorTemperature: 2700 K for decorative and lounge light; 3000 K for practical task light, subject to physical fixture samples.
lighting.colorQuality: Target good color fidelity, preferably CRI 90 or better for selected task/decorative fixtures. Test the actual dimmed lamp or LED against mineral walls, ivory textiles and wood.

controlGroups.name: Cascade chandelier
controlGroups.intent: Independent dimming for the two-story focal fixture.

controlGroups.name: Entry and stair circulation
controlGroups.intent: Useful, separately controlled recessed/ambient light.

controlGroups.intent: Local gentle accent light; avoid blocking clear doors.

electricalCoordination: These are switching/dimming groups, not a claim that each needs a dedicated branch circuit. The electrician determines actual loads, circuiting, required protection and permitted cable routes.
Verify fixture support, electrical box location, dimmer/driver compatibility, flicker and service access before walls close. Do not bury LED drivers or splice points behind finished joinery.
lighting.commissioning: Tune the installed room after dark with the real furniture, curtains and screens. Keep paths and working surfaces useful; render brightness is an illustration, not an illuminance calculation.
lighting.circuits: Cascade chandelier / Entry and stair circulation / Existing small table lamp, if retained

contractorSequence: Verify the plan against the vacant actual house and issue measured elevations, openings and an agreed scope.
Confirm selected furniture and appliances sufficiently to set blocking, wiring, track support and services.

furnitureCoordination.principle: Field-measure the real furniture, openings, delivery route and operating clearances before setting outlets, joinery or tracks. Do not duplicate owned furniture with a fitted replacement.

materials.finish: Premium washable matte acrylic in warm ivory; warm ivory low-sheen trim enamel on painted doors, casings and baseboards.
materials.substratePreparation: Inspect for moisture, movement, uneven patches and incompatible existing coatings. Repair and skim as needed, sand and prime with the selected system. Protect glass, hardware and adjoining stone.
materials.installation: Separate wall coating from door/trim enamel. Use continuous finish boundaries at corners and trim, with no unexplained bright-white patches. Confirm physical color against the oak and walnut.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve the actual material, adjoining finishes and a representative installed sample in daylight and the specified warm evening lighting before ordering the full quantity.
materials.care: Use the selected manufacturer's cleaning and repair instructions; retain product data and matching touch-up material.

materials.finish: Restrained warm mushroom mineral/plaster appearance, with smooth low-contrast movement. Roman Clay is a dry-wall finish option, not a blanket requirement.
materials.substratePreparation: Produce a smooth, sound, properly primed dry wall following the selected coating supplier and the global mineral-finish rule. Resolve cracks, old coating compatibility and uneven absorption before the decorative coat.
materials.installation: Apply the complete selected decorative system to an approved large sample with its intended final sheen. Observe the global dry/wet and material-use boundaries; do not substitute this decorative finish for tile or waterproofing.
materials.sampleApproval: Sample the actual contractor's technique. Reject coarse ridges, peach/pink casts or dramatic clouds inconsistent with the approved room.
materials.care: Follow the finish supplier's dry-area care instructions; plan local repairs with an approved test patch because touch-ups may remain visible.

materials.finish: Matte natural neutral oak with restrained grain and low color variation, matched to the approved second-floor sample. Prefer a suitable engineered product after substrate review.
materials.substratePreparation: Survey existing floor build-up, subfloor condition, flatness, moisture, acoustic requirements, door clearances and transitions. Select the installation and underlayment with the flooring supplier; do not infer requirements from rendered color.
materials.installation: Coordinate continuous levels at thresholds, stair nosings and cabinets. Install per the flooring manufacturer, protect completed floors, and fit neutral loose rugs with a pad expressly compatible with the floor finish.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve a representative plank group beside warm ivory, mushroom mineral and walnut samples. The existing second-floor color is the reference.
materials.care: Use the floor manufacturer's care and felt-protection guidance. Rugs must not trap incompatible rubber, dyes or moisture against the finish.

materials.finish: Warm walnut veneer over a stable furniture-grade carcass, with a matte or low-sheen finish; consistent grain orientation, quiet charcoal interiors and restrained dark hardware.
materials.substratePreparation: Survey wall plumb, floor level, fixing substrate and concealed services. Confirm box condition before deciding whether to reface, reuse or replace. Provide appropriate backing for suspended components.
materials.installation: Use well-detailed modular carcasses, fillers and selected veneer fronts where practical. Keep service panels, ventilation, drawers and LED drivers accessible. Approve an elevation and shop drawings before fabrication.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve veneer grain, end panels, edge finish, sheen, handle treatment and adjoining stone on one representative module.
materials.care: Use the selected manufacturer's cleaning and repair instructions; retain product data and matching touch-up material.

materials.finish: Premium washable matte acrylic in warm ivory; warm ivory low-sheen trim enamel on painted doors, casings and baseboards.
materials.substratePreparation: Inspect for moisture, movement, uneven patches and incompatible existing coatings. Repair and skim as needed, sand and prime with the selected system. Protect glass, hardware and adjoining stone.
materials.installation: Separate wall coating from door/trim enamel. Use continuous finish boundaries at corners and trim, with no unexplained bright-white patches. Confirm physical color against the oak and walnut.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve the actual material, adjoining finishes and a representative installed sample in daylight and the specified warm evening lighting before ordering the full quantity.
materials.care: Use the selected manufacturer's cleaning and repair instructions; retain product data and matching touch-up material.

materials.finish: Restrained warm mushroom mineral/plaster appearance, with smooth low-contrast movement. Roman Clay is a dry-wall finish option, not a blanket requirement.
materials.substratePreparation: Produce a smooth, sound, properly primed dry wall following the selected coating supplier and the global mineral-finish rule. Resolve cracks, old coating compatibility and uneven absorption before the decorative coat.
materials.installation: Apply the complete selected decorative system to an approved large sample with its intended final sheen. Observe the global dry/wet and material-use boundaries; do not substitute this decorative finish for tile or waterproofing.
materials.sampleApproval: Sample the actual contractor's technique. Reject coarse ridges, peach/pink casts or dramatic clouds inconsistent with the approved room.
materials.care: Follow the finish supplier's dry-area care instructions; plan local repairs with an approved test patch because touch-ups may remain visible.

materials.finish: Matte natural neutral oak with restrained grain and low color variation, matched to the approved second-floor sample. Prefer a suitable engineered product after substrate review.
materials.substratePreparation: Survey existing floor build-up, subfloor condition, flatness, moisture, acoustic requirements, door clearances and transitions. Select the installation and underlayment with the flooring supplier; do not infer requirements from rendered color.
materials.installation: Coordinate continuous levels at thresholds, stair nosings and cabinets. Install per the flooring manufacturer, protect completed floors, and fit neutral loose rugs with a pad expressly compatible with the floor finish.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve a representative plank group beside warm ivory, mushroom mineral and walnut samples. The existing second-floor color is the reference.
materials.care: Use the floor manufacturer's care and felt-protection guidance. Rugs must not trap incompatible rubber, dyes or moisture against the finish.

materials.finish: Premium washable matte acrylic in warm ivory; warm ivory low-sheen trim enamel on painted doors, casings and baseboards.
materials.substratePreparation: Inspect for moisture, movement, uneven patches and incompatible existing coatings. Repair and skim as needed, sand and prime with the selected system. Protect glass, hardware and adjoining stone.
materials.installation: Separate wall coating from door/trim enamel. Use continuous finish boundaries at corners and trim, with no unexplained bright-white patches. Confirm physical color against the oak and walnut.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve the actual material, adjoining finishes and a representative installed sample in daylight and the specified warm evening lighting before ordering the full quantity.
materials.care: Use the selected manufacturer's cleaning and repair instructions; retain product data and matching touch-up material.

materials.finish: Restrained warm mushroom mineral/plaster appearance, with smooth low-contrast movement. Roman Clay is a dry-wall finish option, not a blanket requirement.
materials.substratePreparation: Produce a smooth, sound, properly primed dry wall following the selected coating supplier and the global mineral-finish rule. Resolve cracks, old coating compatibility and uneven absorption before the decorative coat.
materials.installation: Apply the complete selected decorative system to an approved large sample with its intended final sheen. Observe the global dry/wet and material-use boundaries; do not substitute this decorative finish for tile or waterproofing.
materials.sampleApproval: Sample the actual contractor's technique. Reject coarse ridges, peach/pink casts or dramatic clouds inconsistent with the approved room.
materials.care: Follow the finish supplier's dry-area care instructions; plan local repairs with an approved test patch because touch-ups may remain visible.

materials.finish: Matte natural neutral oak with restrained grain and low color variation, matched to the approved second-floor sample. Prefer a suitable engineered product after substrate review.
materials.substratePreparation: Survey existing floor build-up, subfloor condition, flatness, moisture, acoustic requirements, door clearances and transitions. Select the installation and underlayment with the flooring supplier; do not infer requirements from rendered color.
materials.installation: Coordinate continuous levels at thresholds, stair nosings and cabinets. Install per the flooring manufacturer, protect completed floors, and fit neutral loose rugs with a pad expressly compatible with the floor finish.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve a representative plank group beside warm ivory, mushroom mineral and walnut samples. The existing second-floor color is the reference.
materials.care: Use the floor manufacturer's care and felt-protection guidance. Rugs must not trap incompatible rubber, dyes or moisture against the finish.

materials.finish: Warm walnut veneer over a stable furniture-grade carcass, with a matte or low-sheen finish; consistent grain orientation, quiet charcoal interiors and restrained dark hardware.
materials.substratePreparation: Survey wall plumb, floor level, fixing substrate and concealed services. Confirm box condition before deciding whether to reface, reuse or replace. Provide appropriate backing for suspended components.
materials.installation: Use well-detailed modular carcasses, fillers and selected veneer fronts where practical. Keep service panels, ventilation, drawers and LED drivers accessible. Approve an elevation and shop drawings before fabrication.
materials.sampleApproval: Approve veneer grain, end panels, edge finish, sheen, handle treatment and adjoining stone on one representative module.

globalStandards.sequence: Work across the vacant house by trade for survey, rough electrical/plumbing/HVAC and blocking before closing walls. Finish substrates and waterproofing before final wall finishes, flooring and coordinated joinery. Install tracks/privacy layers after mounting support is prepared; deliver furniture last and commission each room after dark. The move-in roadmap remains the separate timing authority.
globalStandards.procurement: No piece is represented as purchase-ready solely because it appears in a render. Fresh selected finish/fabric, quantity, actual fit, delivery route and ZIP 20878 availability checks are required. Keep rejected alternatives separate; do not double-order or duplicate owned pieces.
globalStandards.romanClayManufacturerReference: For the Portola Roman Clay option, use properly prepared smooth interior drywall, preferably Level 5, and its specified primer/application system. It is not for wet areas, exterior walls, trim, doors or cabinets. The optional protective topcoat adds protection and some sheen; it does not make the finish waterproof. Final brand and physical color remain unselected.

openDecisions: Exact flooring product, physical wall colors and decorative finish manufacturer.
Final decorative fixture models, dimmer compatibility and actual quantities.
Media active soundbar route versus independently engineered wired AVR route, selected before rough-in.
Owners closet storage reduction and getting-ready bay layout.
Actual-house terrace fireplace/exterior stair inventory and roof/deck condition.
completionRequirements: Measured as-built plan/opening inventory and dated trade scope.
Approved physical finish samples and joinery elevations.
Final equipment/fixture data, actual wiring/control plan and necessary trade/permit reviews.
Site-tested window privacy/blackout coverage and actual door/handle operation.
After-dark lighting/AV commissioning and care/service records.

completionSummary.qaScope: Visual source/plan and paired-camera audit; dimensions, product fit, services, procurement and final construction details remain site-dependent.
